prompt:
Return one complete JSON object.
Return ONLY a JSON hardware interface contract, fixed before generating SysML.
Every pin number below is an EXAMPLE, not an allowed-pin restriction. Preserve the actual requested pins.
Pin mappings written in the ORIGINAL REQUIREMENT are fully valid supplied wiring.
An empty extra pins object means NO OVERRIDES, not missing wiring. For an LED explicitly on D12,
use {kind:"digital_output",pin:12,active_high:true}; do not request another mapping or substitute D13.
The control period is the sampling/scheduling granularity, NOT the LED blink/report period.
Choose a control period of 1..10 ms unless the requirements explicitly specify a different control step.
For 500 ms LED toggles with 10 ms tolerance, use a control step <=10 ms, not 500 or 1000 ms.
An initial-off requirement needs a false output initial value. Never copy initial values from an unrelated example.
Preserve every device and requirement. Do not implement control logic or fabricate sensor values.
Use minimal interfaces: constant LED ON needs one Boolean output (initial true), no enable input or counter.
Initialization deadlines and input/output response deadlines alone do NOT require a clock input or a timer.
Button directly controls LED: one sampled Boolean button input, one Boolean LED output, no elapsed time.
Digital Boolean ports describe MODEL values, not raw voltages. active_high=false means model true at LOW,
model false at HIGH; an active-low button is therefore true when PRESSED and false when RELEASED.
Write meaning in these normalized terms. hardware may describe physical LOW/HIGH wiring, but never say
the model reads false on press for an active-low binding. initial is also a model value.
The server derives model_semantics from each digital binding before freezing; do not author or override it.
Thresholds and business periods belong in model requirements, not hardware bindings.
For business timing use one elapsed_ms input: elapsedMilliseconds, i32, ms, initial 0.
Fading, breathing LEDs, ramps and time-based waveforms also require elapsed_ms, even without the word every.
Never use control_period_ms as a fabricated time increment; real execution intervals may vary.
elapsed_ms ALWAYS means actual time SINCE THE PREVIOUS CONTROL STEP (first step 0).
It is NEVER absolute time since initialization. The SysML model accumulates this delta in persistent state.
Declare the control and sensor sampling periods separately. All output periods equal the control period.
For proportional/scaled/interpolated values use f64 model ports (SysML Real), especially PWM brightness.
The hardware adapter truncates and clamps the final PWM command to 0..255. Integer division in SysML produces Real;
do not force a scaled Real expression through an i32 model output. Use i32 for clocks and actual integer counters.
Use f64 for floating-point ports on this SysML path; its Real scalar mapping is f64, not f32.
Do not invent external enable/reset inputs. Unknown device mappings must be surfaced as an error, never replaced with a different device.
Use exactly these top-level fields:
version: 1, board: "arduino:avr:uno" or "arduino:avr:mega", control_period_ms: positive integer;
Preserve the requested board; never replace Mega with Uno. If none is specified, default to Uno.
Uno: D0..D19, A0..A5 (aliases D14..D19), PWM D3/D5/D6/D9/D10/D11.
Mega: D0..D69, A0..A15 (aliases D54..D69), PWM D2..D13 and D44..D46.
interfaces: [{name: nonreserved C identifier, direction: "input" or "output", type: "bool"/"i32"/"f64",
unit: string, meaning: string, sample_period_ms: positive integer multiple of control_period_ms,
initial: JSON value of matching type, device: string, hardware: description, binding: object}];
requirements: [{id:"R1", text: complete requirement including thresholds/timing/initial behavior, assertion_ids:["expected_behavior_name"]}];
required_dependencies: {outputName:[inputNames]}, required_states: [];
planning_notes: [explicit assumptions or ambiguous timing interpretations].
Requirements and assertion IDs are proposed traceability only, NOT independently verified tests.
required_dependencies describes actual MODEL data/control dependence, not adapter scheduling.
A response deadline such as "display the sampled ADC within 50ms" is enforced by sampling/control periods;
it does not make the displayed value depend on elapsed_ms. Do not invent a clock port or a fake clock dependency.
Explicit initial-silence requirements may produce application-owned startup_checks in the frozen contract.
Those checks evaluate the first MODEL step using declared initial inputs, in addition to adapter initialization.
Hardware binding choices (a catalog, NOT a checklist; create ONLY interfaces required by the original task):
Do not instantiate every example. TM1637 takes its number directly and does NOT use report_trigger or serial_value.
report_trigger is exclusively for serial_value reporting. Do not invent serial interfaces, display triggers or error-surface ports for a display-only task.
input digital_input: {kind:"digital_input",pin:2,pullup:true,active_high:false}, type bool, unit "1";
input analog_input: {kind:"analog_input",pin:"A0",scale:1.0,offset:0.0}, numeric; unit "adc_count" for raw ADC, explicit scale/offset for physical units;
input elapsed_ms: {kind:"elapsed_ms",semantics:"delta_since_previous_step"}, i32 ms, initial 0, sample_period_ms=control_period_ms;
input dht_temperature/dht_humidity: {kind:"dht_temperature",pin:2,sensor:"DHT22",invalid_policy:"hold_last_valid"}, floating point degC/%RH; sample period >=2000 ms; may share a sensor pin;
output digital_output: {kind:"digital_output",pin:13,active_high:true}, bool, unit "1";
output pwm_output: {kind:"pwm_output",pin:9,scale:1.0,offset:0.0}, numeric; unit "pwm_count" for 0..255; use a PWM pin on the selected board;
output servo_angle: {kind:"servo_angle",pin:2,invalid_policy:"hold_last_valid"}, numeric deg, initial 0..180; use f64 for proportional angles.
Positional servos use Servo.h with default 544..2400 us endpoints. The adapter truncates valid 0..180 degree commands to integer degrees; invalid/nonfinite commands hold the last valid angle. It provides no measured position feedback.
Servo outputs may use any available digital pin 0..63 (including analog aliases); no PWM pin is required. Mega D64..D69/A10..A15 are unsupported by Servo's AVR pin storage.
Uno supports 12 servos and consumes Timer1 (PWM D9/D10 unavailable). Mega groups of 12 consume Timer5, Timer1, Timer3, Timer4 in that order, disabling PWM on D44/D45/D46, then D11/D12, then D2/D3/D5, then D6/D7/D8. Preserve requested wiring and report conflicts.
Declare one angle output for EACH physical servo, even when two share the same desired angle. Keep ADC-to-angle mapping, speed, sequences, pauses and motion timing in SysML; servo bindings cannot contain speed/easing/duration logic.
This binding supports positional servos only, not continuous-rotation speed control or custom pulse calibration. Never substitute pwm_output or digital_output for a servo.
output tone_output: {kind:"tone_output",pin:6,invalid_policy:"silence"}, i32 Hz; 0 stops, 31..65535 commands the pitch, other values silence.
Use tone_output for passive buzzer sound, never replace sound with a static digital pin or a PWM duty cycle.
The MODEL sets frequency to 0 when silent and to the requested pitch when sounding; duration, repetition and pause logic stay in the MODEL using elapsed_ms.
Only one tone_output is supported. AVR tone uses Timer2: it cannot coexist with PWM on Uno D3/D11 or Mega D9/D10. Preserve explicit wiring; report conflicts instead of rewiring.
output report_trigger: {kind:"report_trigger"}, bool, unit "1", consumed by serial_value;
output serial_value: {kind:"serial_value",trigger:"reportDue",label:"Temperature: ",baud:115200}; the trigger is a Boolean model output; no adapter report timer.
output tm1637_number: {kind:"tm1637_number",clk_pin:4,dio_pin:5,brightness:7,leading_zero:false,invalid_policy:"blank"}, i32; one signed four-digit number, -999..9999 (0..9999 with leading_zero=true).
Use the actual CLK/DIO wiring, never create two independent scalar outputs for the two bus pins. One output selects the number displayed; multiple values shown alternately must be selected by SysML state/timing.
Analog-to-display scaling and rounding belong in SysML (e.g. RealFunctions::floor(adc*9999.0/1023.0)), never in display bindings. Units describe the displayed quantity.
This binding supports numeric four-digit display only, not arbitrary text, decimal points or a display library timer. Report unsupported requirements explicitly.
All pins must honor supplied mappings. Inputs must be real hardware samples or elapsed time.
Each requirement must be retained even if unsupported; never silently drop devices to pass validation.
For hardware outside this binding set return {"unsupported":[descriptions]}.

Original requirements:
蜂鸣器（D6）每 3 秒响一次，按钮（D2）暂停/恢复
验收约定：D6使用无源蜂鸣器，音调1000Hz，每次持续100ms；初始运行且静音，累计运行3000ms后首次发声，此后每累计运行3000ms开始一次。D2使用INPUT_PULLUP，低电平按下沿切换暂停/恢复，长按及松开不切换。暂停立即静音，保留计时和剩余鸣叫时长，恢复后继续，不能重新开始完整周期。响应及鸣叫时间容差20ms。
Supplied pins:
{}
Required target board: arduino:avr:uno
Authoritative pin names explicitly provided in the original requirement (use these, even if extra pins is empty):
["D2", "D6"]
The requirement includes time-dependent behavior: an elapsed_ms input is REQUIRED. Include a complete interface such as {"name": "elapsedMilliseconds", "direction": "input", "type": "i32", "unit": "ms", "initial": 0, "sample_period_ms": 10, "meaning": "Actual delta since previous control step", "device": "clock", "hardware": "millis delta", "binding": {"kind": "elapsed_ms", "semantics": "delta_since_previous_step"}}. Set its sample_period_ms equal to the chosen control_period_ms. initial belongs outside binding.

Return one complete JSON object.
Return one JSON object with exactly controller and req_test_map.
The application assembles the full SysML package and ALL external declarations from the frozen interface contract.
Do NOT return system_sysml2, package text, external declarations, a second system instance, or package-level bindings.
The assembled SysML is checked by the reference validator, then compiled from its semantic model.

controller schema:
{
 "states": [{"name":"internalName", "type":"bool|i32|f64", "initial":"SysML constant expression"}],
 "updates": [ordered statements],
 "outputs": {"EXACT_CONTRACT_OUTPUT_NAME":"SysML expression"}
}
Only states, updates and outputs are required. Start from this minimal schema.
For edge toggles and periodic pulses whose semantics match the requirement, use the typed components below
instead of reimplementing their internal state updates. They expand into ordinary SysML states/actions,
and the ENTIRE expanded model still passes reference parsing, IR compilation and interface checks.
Optional components: ordered array of either:
{"kind":"edge_toggle","name":"run","input":"pressed","edge":"rising","initial":true,"previous_input":false}
{"kind":"periodic_pulse","name":"beep","delta":"deltaMs","enabled":"component_run_value","period_ms":3000,"pulse_ms":100,"first_pulse":"after_period","pause":"preserve"}
Each component exports one read-only Boolean: component_NAME_value. Never redeclare or assign any component_ name.
edge_toggle: input is a declared Boolean input or earlier component export; edge is rising or falling;
initial is the initial toggled value; previous_input is the initial edge memory. Both are JSON Booleans.
A normalized active-low button is true when PRESSED, so press-edge requires rising, not falling.
periodic_pulse: delta names the actual i32 millisecond delta input; enabled is "true", "false", a Boolean input,
or an earlier component export. period_ms is START-TO-START active time, including the sounding interval.
pulse_ms must be 1..period_ms. first_pulse is after_period (initial silence) or immediate (initial pulse).
pause=preserve freezes phase/remaining pulse; pause=reset restarts timing when enabled again.
Output is always false while disabled. Delta belongs to the preceding interval: pause counts the interval
ending at the press, resume excludes the preceding paused interval. The first adapter delta is 0.
Components execute in array order BEFORE free-form updates. Outputs observe the resulting values.
Use the ORIGINAL requirement's parameters, edge, initial mode and pause policy. These are choices, not defaults.
If these two components do not express the required behavior, retain the ordinary states/updates schema;
never alter a requirement to fit a component. Components do not read pins, drive devices or format text.
Optional fields, ONLY when the requirement needs decomposition:
calculations: array of {name, type, expression}; parts: array of {name, definition};
bindings: array of {left, right}, each endpoint a declared scalar name or part.scalar reference, never a literal;
definitions: array of {name, inputs:[{name,type}], output_ports:[{name,type}], body:{states,updates,outputs}}.
Module bodies may also have calculations, parts, bindings and components. Never copy an unrelated module from a schema example.
Root inputs/output names and types are ALREADY supplied by the contract; never redeclare them in states/calculations.
Each output appears exactly once in outputs. Each state has an initial value and a type.
Do not introduce counters, enable/reset inputs or modules unless required by the actual behavior.

Statement forms (use JSON objects, not raw action text):
{"assign":"internalStateName","value":"SysML expression"}
{"if":"Boolean SysML expression","then":[statements],"else":[statements]}
else may be omitted. An empty then/else list means no state change in that branch; its condition is still checked.
The renderer generates first start/then syntax and preserves list order, including explicit no-op branches.
Assignments target only initialized internal states (or qualified part states). Root outputs are derived expressions, not assignment targets.
Outputs read state AFTER all ordered updates. All performed behavior must form one control step; no concurrent action schedules.
Assignments take effect IMMEDIATELY: each later statement sees earlier writes, not a snapshot of old state.
For edge detection evaluate pressed and not previousPressed BEFORE updating previousPressed; update that memory LAST.
For start/stop timing reset the accumulator and output at the transition; stopping must not leave a stale ON output.

Simple expressions are strings using not/and/or; + - * /; == != < <= > >=.
Literal operands, state initial values and conditional branches may also be JSON Booleans or finite numbers.
true/false remain Boolean, integer literals remain Integer and decimal literals such as 1.0 remain Real;
these do not bypass reference type checking. null, NaN and Infinity are not expressions.
Boolean negation may also use {"not":"Boolean expression"}; it is rendered as SysML not and fully type-checked.
Structured operators are also accepted: {"and":["enabled",{"not":"paused"}]} and {">=":["elapsed","3000"]}.
and/or/xor accept 2..256 expression operands; == != < <= > >= + - * / accept exactly two.
Operands may be expression strings or nested expression objects; their order and parentheses are preserved.
Do not use function-style and(a,b)/or(a,b)/xor(a,b) strings; use infix strings or these structured objects.
CONDITIONAL VALUE EXPRESSIONS MUST use an object: {"if":"condition","then":"yesValue","else":"noValue"}.
Use this object anywhere an expression is accepted (output, assignment value, calculation, or nested expression).
Each branch is an expression string or another conditional expression object. The application generates the SysML conditional syntax.
This differs from an if STATEMENT, whose then/else fields are arrays of actions. An expression never contains action arrays.
No C !, &&, ||, % or raw ternary strings. No statements, comments or declarations inside expression strings.
For input gating use {"if":"pressed","then":"sampledValue * 255.0 / 1023.0","else":"0.0"} as the Real output value.
Toggled state is Boolean, not Integer. Division produces Real; do not put division results into Integer state.
For a required Integer output use RealFunctions::floor(realExpression), e.g.
{"if":"pressed","then":"RealFunctions::floor(adc * 255.0 / 1023.0)","else":"0"}.
floor rounds toward negative infinity; its result must fit signed 32 bits. Other function calls are unsupported.
Timing inputs with binding.kind=elapsed_ms are actual delta SINCE THE PREVIOUS CONTROL STEP, first value 0.
Accumulate the delta in state for business timing; never invent a constant clock increment.
digital_input with active_high=false is ALREADY normalized: true means pressed/active. Do not invert it twice.
Hardware sampling and driving follow the contract; control, thresholds, timing and state transitions must remain in this model.
For servo_angle the output is a commanded angle in degrees, normally Real for a proportional mapping.
Compute every physical servo output from the specified sampled inputs; multiple servos may share an expression but each declared output is required.
The adapter only sends angles: any requested speed, motion sequence, pause or time interval must be implemented by model state and elapsed time.
Servo readback is not a measured physical position. Do not invent a sensor input or replace a potentiometer with a constant.
For tone_output the output is an Integer frequency in Hz: 0 means silent, a positive in-range value is the pitch.
Implement all beep start/stop times, pulse duration, repetition and pause/resume state in this controller.
The adapter generates only the carrier and never adds a beep timer or pulse duration.
If the frozen contract includes startup_checks, the model's FIRST step with declared initial inputs
must produce those expected outputs. Setting only the adapter initial output does not satisfy that check.
If it includes pause_checks, a normalized press rising edge toggles the specified initial running mode;
the output must equal expected whenever paused, including while held, after release and in a partly completed pulse.
These application-owned assertions are derived from explicit public requirements or supplied by the caller.
Preserve them exactly. Passing them covers only those properties; all other timing and behavior is still required.
Frozen periodic_checks test explicit start-to-start period, pulse width, first pulse and any press-edge pause policy using public synthetic traces.
Advance period time through BOTH sound and silence. Preserve remaining phase and pulse during preserve-mode pause; reset only if the contract explicitly requires reset.
Assignments are immediate: after remaining := remaining - delta, compare remaining <= 0; subtracting delta again in the guard tests a different value.
These checks do not replace independent final tests. Never remove an assertion or change its timing to make a model pass.










Pause/resume and pulse timing are distinct state concepts. For a period measured start-to-start in ACTIVE running time,
advance the period counter throughout BOTH sounding and silent portions whenever running. Advancing it only while silent
silently changes the required period to period + pulseDuration. Freeze the whole active-time phase only when paused.
Example: initially running but silent; first pulse after 3000ms active time, repeated every 3000ms active time,
100ms pulse at 1000Hz; press edge pauses/resumes preserving phase, including a partly completed pulse.
Adapt names, all numeric parameters, initial mode and pause/reset policy to the actual requirement.
{"states":[],"updates":[],
 "components":[{"kind":"edge_toggle","name":"run","input":"pressed","edge":"rising","initial":true,"previous_input":false},
               {"kind":"periodic_pulse","name":"beep","delta":"deltaMs","enabled":"component_run_value",
                "period_ms":3000,"pulse_ms":100,"first_pulse":"after_period","pause":"preserve"}],
 "outputs":{"frequency":{"if":"component_beep_value","then":"1000","else":"0"}}}
The component's first_pulse policy prevents a spurious pulse at startup. The adapter still samples real elapsed time even during pause;
only the model decides whether that delta advances business time. No hidden test timeline belongs in this controller.


req_test_map MUST be an OBJECT, never an array. Its complete shape is:
{"requirements_to_testpoints":[{"requirement_id":"R1","requirement_text":"original requirement","test_point_id":"T1","test_method":"trace","stimulus":"input","oracle":"expected output"}]}
req_test_map.requirements_to_testpoints must be non-empty. Each row requires requirement_id, requirement_text,
test_point_id, test_method, stimulus, oracle. Preserve ALL frozen requirement IDs. These proposed tests are not proof of correctness.

Normative model/electrical boundary (derived from the SAME binding used by the adapter):
[{"name": "buttonPauseToggle", "direction": "input", "pin": 2, "initial_model_value": false, "kind": "digital_boolean", "true_level": "LOW", "false_level": "HIGH"}]
For each input, the model Boolean is true exactly when the pin is at true_level; it is false at false_level. For each output, model true drives true_level and false drives false_level. initial_model_value is a MODEL value, not a raw pin voltage. Meaning/hardware prose may describe physical levels; do not reinterpret those levels as model Boolean values. For an active-low pressed button, LOW already becomes true before the model runs: test that input directly for pressed, and detect a rising MODEL edge for press. Do not invert again or change the binding to fit a mistaken interpretation. Control and state stay in SysML.
